**<mark>ICSG PRESS RELEASE                                                  Date Issued: 21</mark>**<sup>**st**</sup> **<mark>July 2011</mark>** 



# **Copper: Preliminary Data for April 2011** 

The International Copper Study Group (ICSG) released preliminary data for April 2011 world copper supply and demand in its July 2011 Copper Bulletin. The Bulletin is available for sale upon request. 

According to preliminary ICSG data, the refined copper market balance for April 2011 showed a production deficit of 36,000 metric tonnes (t). However, when making seasonal adjustments for world refined production and usage, April showed a surplus of 46,000 t. The apparent refined copper balance for the first four months of 2011, including revisions to data previously presented, indicates a production deficit of 69,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 46,000 t). This compares with a production deficit of 57,000 t (a seasonally adjusted surplus of 70,000 t) in the same period of 2010. 

During the first four months of 2011, world apparent usage grew by 1.2% compared with that in the same period of 2010. A 7% decline in apparent usage* at the world biggest copper using country, China, was more than offset by growth in other parts of the world, including Russia (growth of 89%),  the European Union (2.2%), and the United States (2.2%). China’s apparent usage decline reflected a 40% decrease in net imports of refined copper from those in the same period of 2010, while the increase in Russia’s apparent usage reflected a 63% decline in net refined exports. Usage in the United States and the EU continued to recover from the recession, although now at a slower pace than during 2010. On a regional basis, usage grew by 5% in Africa, 3.7% in the Americas, 9.3% in Europe and 38% in Oceania, and declined by 2.8% in Asia. 

World mine production grew by around 2% in the first four months of 2011 compared with that in the same period of 2010: Concentrate production grew by 3% while solvent extraction-electrowinning (SX-EW) declined by 1.5%. In part, this modest net increase reflects operational constraints that reduced production in 2010 in Australia and Mexico. Production in Chile, the world’s leading producer, was down by 1.4%.  Production was also down in other major producers, including the United States (-4.5%), Indonesia (-18%) and the Democratic Republic of Congo (-16%). On a regional basis, mine production increased by 0.7% in the Americas, 5.7% in Europe and 22% in Oceania, but decreased by around 0.5% in both Africa and Asia.  The mine capacity utilization rate increased slightly in April and the average for the first four months of 2011 was unchanged from that in the same period of 2010. 

During the first four months of 2011, world refined production grew by 1% as compared with that in the same period of 2010: Primary production remained practically unchanged and secondary production (from scrap) increased by 4.7%. Production increases of 57% in Australia (r

ecovery from low 2010 level), 12% in China and 6% in India were partially offset by declines in Chile (-4%), the United Sates (-11%), Canada (-28%) and Japan (-16%). Refined production capacity utilization in the first four months of 2011 was around 78% as compared with 79% in the same period of 2010. The average LME cash price for June 2011 was US$9,045.43 per tonne, up from the May 2011 average of US$8,927.05 per tonne. The 2011 high and low copper prices through the end of June were US$10,148 and US$8,536.5 per tonne, respectively, and the average was US$9,397.64 per tonne. As of the end of June, copper stocks held at the major metal exchanges (LME, COMEX, SHFE) totalled 616,912 t, an increase of 48,730 t from stocks held at the end of December 2010. Compared to the May levels, stocks were down at the three exchanges.
